anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
Funds and/or vehicles advised and/or managed by affiliates of Blackstone Private Credit Strategies LLC (**Blackstone Credit**) propose to exchange their existing debt interest in Discovery Education, Inc. (**Discovery**) for new debt and a significant, but less than a majority, equity interest in full satisfaction of such existing debt interest (the **Acquisition**).

Blackstone Credit is part of the Credit & Insurance segment of Blackstone Inc. (together with any of its affiliates or affiliated investment funds, **Blackstone**).

Blackstone is a US-based investment management firm, incorporated under the laws of Delaware, United States. Each company in its investment portfolio is independently managed and financed and has different investors (although the investors in different investment funds may overlap). Each Blackstone portfolio company has its own board of directors, which generally also include Blackstone representatives.

Blackstone currently controls Renaissance Learning, Inc. (**Renaissance**), a US-based provider of cloud-based software for the pre-kindergarten to year 12 education sector. Renaissance offers learning resources and tools to support students and teachers.

Discovery is a US-based company that provides digital learning resources for kindergarten to year 12 (K-12) students, educators and schools across science, math, literacy and social studies. Discovery’s key offerings are companion educational platforms, supplementary learning resources, and subject-based learning solutions.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of K–12 digital
education resources to customers in Australia is expected to
be low and the increase in share of supply arising from the
Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of K–12 digital education
resources to customers in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
